# Introduction

scdRs is a native R implementation of scDRS (single-cell
disease-relevance score; Zhang, Hou et al., *Nature Genetics* 2022). It
scores each cell of a single-cell RNA-seq data set for excess expression
of a disease gene set (e.g. from GWAS) compared with matched control gene
sets.

The package is under development. This vignette will describe the full
workflow once it is implemented.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("scdRs")
```

# Example data

The package ships the toy data of the original scDRS (2,500 genes,
30 cells). Here it is loaded into a `SingleCellExperiment`.

```{r toydata, message = FALSE}
library(SingleCellExperiment)

ext <- system.file("extdata", package = "scdRs")
expr <- as.matrix(read.csv(file.path(ext, "toydata_logexpr.csv.gz"),
    row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
cells <- read.csv(file.path(ext, "toydata_cell_metadata.csv"),
    row.names = 1)
cov <- read.csv(file.path(ext, "toydata_covariates.csv"), row.names = 1)
cells$covariate <- cov[rownames(cells), "covariate"]

sce <- SingleCellExperiment(
    assays = list(logcounts = expr[, rownames(cells)]),
    colData = cells
)
sce
table(sce$cell_type)
```

The disease gene sets are stored in the scDRS `.gs` format: one trait
per line, with a comma-separated list of genes.

```{r genesets}
gs <- read.delim(file.path(ext, "toydata_mouse.gs"))
gs$TRAIT
length(strsplit(gs$GENESET, ",")[[1]])
```

# Citation

If you use scdRs, please cite the original scDRS paper:

```{r citation}
citation("scdRs")
```
